verifier_constraints.snapshot_identity: every present product_snapshot_digest is unique within the package; contract-bearing snapshots always carry one

verifier_constraints.subset_identity: every item equals exactly one formats_to_provide item after RFC 8785 canonicalization and carries the identical product_snapshot_digest when present

verifier_constraints.package_snapshot_product: every formats_to_provide and formats_pending item product_id equals this readback package product_id; a contract-bearing snapshot requires the enclosing product_id

notes: Task response schemas (e.g., get-products-response.json) define ONLY the body fields; protocol-layer fields live on this envelope.

- MCP: envelope fields and task-body fields are siblings at the root of the tool response. The `payload` object is NOT serialized as a nested key — its body fields are flattened to the root alongside `status`, `context_id`, `context`, etc. This matches MCP's native `structuredContent` convention and is what shipping SDKs (@adcp/client) emit. Conformant MCP receivers parse from the flat root; receivers that expect a nested `payload` key MUST migrate.

- A2A 1.0 with the AdCP profile extension: `task.status.state` carries the transport invocation lifecycle used to select the extraction location; `task.contextId` carries `context_id`, while `task.id` is an independent A2A transport identifier. The complete AdCP response, including its protocol-level `status` and any application-layer `task_id`, is canonically carried in `task.artifacts[0].parts[].DataPart` on final states; `task.status.message.parts[].DataPart` is the fallback container used only for interim A2A states (working, native submitted, input-required) where no final artifact has been emitted yet. For a structured AdCP business rejection or Submitted response, A2A is `completed` while the DataPart carries `status: rejected` or `status: submitted` because the handler invocation succeeded. An AdCP `task_id` MUST NOT be copied into artifact metadata or inferred from `task.id`. Receivers MUST prefer artifacts when present and MUST NOT overwrite a DataPart's status with the A2A state. See `a2a-profile-extension.mdx` and `a2a-response-extraction.mdx` for the full binding and extraction algorithm.

- REST: envelope fields MAY ride on HTTP headers (e.g., `X-AdCP-Status`, `X-AdCP-Context-Id`) or as JSON body siblings; body fields appear at the JSON body root. Implementers choosing the header path SHOULD also mirror to body siblings for non-streaming callers.

Across all three: envelope and body fields are conceptually a single response object. A task response schema MAY declare body fields with the same name as envelope fields (e.g., `errors[]` body-level for per-record validation results vs envelope-level for fatal task failure) and the two MUST be treated as distinct fields by name within their respective namespaces — see `error-handling.mdx#envelope-vs-payload-errors-the-two-layer-model`.

`status` is REQUIRED on the conceptual AdCP response across all transports. On MCP and REST it appears as a sibling field at the JSON root (or `structuredContent` root for MCP). On A2A it is carried inside the authoritative DataPart alongside the task body; `task.status.state` separately carries the A2A transport lifecycle and selects where that DataPart is found. Receivers MUST preserve the DataPart status when present. The schema-level `required: [status]` enforces the post-extraction AdCP shape. `payload` remains intentionally NOT required — it is a documentary grouping construct, never a required wire field. See `mcp-guide.mdx` and `a2a-guide.mdx` for the wire-level patterns receivers MUST implement.
Receivers MUST handle absence of an envelope field (e.g., `replayed` omitted) as the field's documented default — see each field's `default` clause.

verifier_constraints.resolved_purchase_terms: Each purchase carries resolved start_time and end_time. Applicable measurement_terms and performance_standards are copied from the published offer or negotiated successor; omission means no such terms apply.

verifier_constraints.direct_purchase_terms: On buy_products, supplied start_time, end_time, measurement_terms, and performance_standards MUST exactly match the selected published offer; omission inherits that offer.
verifier_constraints.accepted_snapshot_terms: Inside canonical-proposal.commercial_terms, each purchase MUST carry resolved start_time and end_time and MUST preserve every applicable measurement term and performance standard. Omission of measurement_terms or performance_standards means the accepted offer declared none.

x-adcp-validation.description: JSON Schema draft-07 cannot compare values across sibling arrays. Conformance tooling MUST reject any place identity present in both geo_places and geo_places_exclude. Catalog version is deliberately not part of place identity: a stable ID cannot be both included and excluded by assigning different versions.
Every value_labels key MUST also appear in values. JSON Schema draft-07 cannot express this sibling-field key membership constraint, so conformance tooling must enforce it.

verifier_constraints.allowed_statuses: Every value is a non-terminal MediaBuy status. The current buy projection omits the action outside these statuses without extinguishing the negotiated right.
verifier_constraints.constraint_currency: Every monetary constraint currency equals the commercial terms purchase currency.
verifier_constraints.constraint_consistency: Minimum result does not exceed maximum result; earliest timestamp does not exceed latest timestamp.

x-adcp-validation.description: `dimensions[]` is an array for readable intersection syntax, but `kind` is a logical set key. JSON Schema draft-07 cannot express unique-by-property for this array shape, so conformance tooling should reject repeated `kind` values.

x-adcp-validation.binding_authorization: For managed delivery, destination_ref and any recipient identity MUST be bound to the stable authenticated caller, and proof of recipient/destination control plus disclosure authorization MUST precede ready. This account configuration separately binds and authorizes the resolved account/feed/scope; possession of a reusable destination_ref grants no account authority. Core readiness has no destination proof step.
x-adcp-validation.coverage: current_coverage evaluates the selected offering after product/package and account-specific constraints. A full configuration cannot be ready with a partial, none, or unknown nonempty denominator. allow_partial readiness does not convert partial coverage to full or weaken the report definition.
x-adcp-validation.period_eligibility: Only complete schedule periods whose period.start is at or after activated_at are eligible. A mid-period activation begins at the next boundary; periods are never clipped. On voluntary deactivation, publication_stopped_at MUST be a schedule boundary at or after deactivated_at. Periods whose start is before that boundary remain obligations and may complete afterward; periods whose start is at or after it MUST NOT be created.
x-adcp-validation.revocation: Voluntary deactivation stops new obligations/publication at publication_stopped_at. A still-authorized principal may retain a producer-hosted historical share only through seller_managed_access_ends_at. Caller authorization loss, account closure, or recipient revocation overrides that window and terminates seller-controlled transport access and provider grants within authorization_revocation_seconds. For buyer-owned destinations, the seller revokes write ability but cannot revoke the buyer's access to bytes already delivered; buyer retention governs those copies.
x-adcp-validation.safe_setup_url: Reject URL userinfo, non-HTTPS, credential-like query/fragment values, redirects or origins outside the seller/named provider allowlist. Agents must surface the URL for explicit human action without fetching or interpreting its content.
x-adcp-validation.core_readiness: A configuration selecting a Core offering (no method) reaches ready without any destination, provider grant, or setup action: validation covers scope, schedule, and offering match only. destination_ref and destination proof are required for ready when and only when the selected offering declares a method.

x-adcp-validation.tier_boundaries: method is present when and only when the selected offering declares one. A configuration selecting a Core (API-delivered) offering involves no destination, manifest, canonicalization, or receipt machinery.
x-adcp-validation.offering_applicability: Resolve the seller-wide offering through every selected product's reporting_capabilities.reporting_delivery_offering_ids, then apply account, seat, credential, provider, and API constraints. Seller-wide advertisement alone is not proof that an individual package is eligible.
x-adcp-validation.coverage_requirement: A full configuration MUST NOT become ready for a current nonempty partial, none, or unknown scope and any later incomplete period becomes action_required with REPORTING_COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE. allow_partial MAY become ready when some scope is covered, but every obligation and revision freezes exact coverage and aggregate consumers keep the partial label.

x-adcp-validation.tier_boundaries: An offering without method is Core: delivered through existing API transports, no destination, manifest, or canonicalization knowledge required. method requires the managed_delivery capability. reconciliation_mode consumer_receipt requires the reconciled_billing capability, and such offerings MUST carry the full canonicalization_* contract in reporting_profile. delivery_only offerings omit canonicalization.
x-adcp-validation.safe_schema_fetch: schema_uri, canonicalization_uri, and report_definition_uri origins must be the authenticated seller, the named provider, or an AdCP registry. Reject userinfo, IP literals, localhost, private/reserved DNS results, redirects, and DNS/connect-target mismatch; pin resolution, cap bytes/time, require the expected content type, verify the corresponding SHA-256 before parsing, and cache by digest. The canonicalization and report-definition documents MUST validate against their AdCP contract schemas. The fetched row schema's $schema MUST equal schema_dialect, whose metaschema is SDK-bundled and never network-fetched. Before compiling with no network-capable resolver installed, recursively reject every $ref not beginning with #, all $dynamicRef and $recursiveRef keywords, cyclic references, excessive depth/node count, oversized regexes, and unsupported vocabularies. Fetched content and annotations are untrusted data, never agent or LLM instructions.
x-adcp-validation.snapshot_declaration: A snapshot claim is the atomic combination of supported_finality containing snapshot, this exact schedule, report definition/profile, and delivery method. Sellers MUST NOT imply a faster snapshot cadence from polling, webhook, or transport support that is not advertised by such an offering.

x-adcp-validation.algorithm: adcp_jcs_rows_v1 rejects duplicate JSON object keys, non-finite numbers, lone Unicode surrogates, missing/non-scalar primary keys, and duplicate primary-key tuples. Validate every row against the pinned row schema; do not normalize Unicode. RFC 8785-encode each primary-key value array and sort rows by unsigned lexicographic comparison of those UTF-8 bytes. RFC 8785-encode each complete row, then emit the UTF-8 bytes for '[' + the encoded rows joined by ',' + ']'. SHA-256 is computed over exactly those bytes.
x-adcp-validation.binding: schema_sha256 and primary_keys MUST exactly equal the selected offering. Golden-vector names MUST be unique across empty_report, ordering_encoding, and additional. empty_report is the exact [] case. ordering_encoding is non-trivial: its input row order differs from canonical primary-key order and its object member order differs from JCS order. SDKs MUST strictly base64-decode canonical_utf8_base64, reproduce every golden vector's exact bytes and sha256, and reject any mismatch before using the contract.

x-adcp-validation.installed_schedule_match: period_duration, alignment, and delivery_sla MUST equal the installed configuration. For fixed billing_cycle offerings, period_anchor and period_timezone MUST also equal it. For configurable billing_cycle offerings, the installed configuration supplies both values. utc and account_timezone use the normative origins in reporting-schedule.json, so even multi-unit durations have one independently derivable phase.

x-adcp-validation.period_generation: Producer and consumer MUST derive the same ordered half-open intervals from period_duration, alignment, period_anchor, and period_timezone when applicable. utc alignment uses 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z as interval zero. account_timezone uses 1970-01-01T00:00:00 in the account's resolved IANA timezone as interval zero. billing_cycle uses its explicit period_anchor expressed in period_timezone. Every boundary is calculated directly from that origin and the interval ordinal by multiplying each ISO 8601 duration component by the ordinal and applying years, months, days, hours, minutes, then seconds. Calendar durations use local civil-time arithmetic in the selected IANA timezone, including DST transitions; they are not converted to fixed seconds. Month/year addition preserves the origin's local day and time, clamping to the target month's final valid day when necessary. A nonexistent local boundary advances by the timezone gap; an ambiguous local boundary uses the earlier offset. Thus a clamped February boundary does not shift a March 31 anchor.

x-adcp-validation.authorization: Bind every destination_ref to the stable authenticated caller. Reuse across that caller's accounts is permitted only after each account configuration independently verifies disclosure authority for its feed and media-buy scope. Reject unknown, unauthorized, and cross-caller refs indistinguishably.
x-adcp-validation.destination_proof: Before ready, prove destination control and caller authority for every selected account, feed, and media-buy scope. A proof-bound coordinate or delivery-contract change creates a new destination_ref; old references remain stable for retained configurations and history. Revoke grants when the configuration, caller authorization, or account becomes inactive.

x-adcp-validation.authorization: Bind every destination_ref to the stable authenticated caller. Reuse across that caller's accounts is permitted only after each account configuration independently verifies disclosure authority for its feed and media-buy scope. Reject unknown, unauthorized, and cross-caller refs indistinguishably.
x-adcp-validation.recipient_proof: Before ready, prove recipient control and caller authority to disclose every selected account, feed, and media-buy scope. A proof-bound recipient or delivery-contract change creates a new destination_ref; old references remain stable for retained configurations and history. Voluntary configuration deactivation stops new publication but may preserve still-authorized historical access through seller_managed_access_ends_at. Caller authorization loss, account closure, or recipient revocation overrides that window and revokes the grant within authorization_revocation_seconds.

x-adcp-validation.retention: expires_at MUST be no earlier than the owning obligation.resource_retained_until and publication plus advertised resource_retention_days. A completed obligation cannot rely on deterministic rematerialization in place of a readable exact resource.

x-adcp-validation.partition: The four media-buy classification arrays MUST be pairwise disjoint and their union MUST equal media_buy_ids. The three package classification arrays MUST be pairwise disjoint and their union MUST equal package_ids. Every limitation media_buy_id and package_id MUST belong to those denominators.
x-adcp-validation.status: full requires every media buy to be fully covered and every package covered; the explicit empty denominator is full. partial requires at least one covered package or fully covered media buy and at least one partial, unsupported, or unknown item. none requires a nonempty denominator, no covered item, at least one unsupported item, and no unknown item. unknown requires a nonempty denominator, no covered item, and at least one unknown item.
x-adcp-validation.aggregation: Metrics computed only over covered_package_ids MUST be labeled partial whenever status is not full and MUST NOT be represented as complete media-buy or campaign totals. Implementations MUST NOT weaken the selected report definition to create an undeclared lowest-common-denominator profile.

external:enums/media-buy-valid-action.js.x-deprecated-enum-values-doc: Coarse legacy values retained for backwards compatibility with 3.x sellers. Each rolls up to one or more finer-grained values published in 3.1 (see `enumMetadata[<value>].rollup`). Removed in 4.0.

enumMetadata.$comment: Structured per-action metadata. Each entry carries `update_fields` (the `update_media_buy` request fields this action covers, as dotted paths rooted at the request body) and optional `rollup` for legacy coarse values that are superseded by finer-grained vocabulary. SDKs MUST consume this block to dispatch update_media_buy requests rather than parsing the field-mapping table in the update_media_buy task-reference doc; the doc is the human-readable mirror of this normative data. Deprecated values are marked at the top-level `x-deprecated-enum-values` (repo convention); SDKs and codegen MAY hide deprecated values from caller-facing surfaces when any value in the entry's `rollup` array is present in the same `available_actions[]` or `valid_actions[]` payload.

verifier_constraints.change_term_link: When change_term_id is present, it resolves to the accepted proposal change term governing this action.
verifier_constraints.legacy_alias_agreement: When both change_term_id and deprecated terms_ref are emitted as proposal-term links, their values are identical.

verifier_constraints.change_term_link: When change_term_id is present, it resolves to exactly one accepted_proposal.commercial_terms.change_terms[].term_id whose action, service_mode, and processing_sla agree with this projection.
verifier_constraints.legacy_alias_agreement: When change_term_id and deprecated terms_ref are both present and terms_ref is being used as the proposal-term link, their values are identical. A 3.1 terms_ref with no accepted change term remains an opaque legacy commercial pointer and MUST NOT be reinterpreted as authority.

verifier_constraints.tracker_execution_contract_digest: lowercase-hex SHA-256 of RFC 8785 canonical JSON of tracker_execution_contract alone, with transmitted values and no materialized defaults
verifier_constraints.product_snapshot_digest: lowercase-hex SHA-256 of RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the closed object {product_id, format, placement_refs?, execution_vast_version?, execution_daast_version?, tracker_execution_contract_digest?}; format contains every transmitted ProductFormatDeclaration field and excludes every package-only field
verifier_constraints.placement_order: placement_refs sorted by publisher_domain then placement_id using ascending transmitted UTF-8 bytes without Unicode normalization
verifier_constraints.execution_version: when a first-class VAST or DAAST tracker selector has no sibling exact-version delivery document, the matching execution_*_version is required and belongs to the selected option acceptance set
verifier_constraints.immutability: changing selected format, placement set, execution version, or tracker contract requires a replacement package_id; never mutate this snapshot in place

verifier_constraints.translation_chain_closure: every translate_to_native entry must have an exact matching resolve_value entry for its translation_target in this same array

x-adcp-validation.version_sets: For one non-version selector identity, version sets must be identical or disjoint; overlapping unequal sets are invalid.
x-adcp-validation.asset_normalization: Before selector matching, omitted pixel_tracker.method becomes img, omitted VAST/DAAST target becomes linear, and offset on a non-progress asset is ignored and removed. Existing 3.x asset schemas remain structurally permissive; the selector schema supplies the closed event/target matrix for contract matching.
x-adcp-validation.format_slot_satisfiability: Every asset_type named by honored MUST have at least one matching first-class slot in the effective selected canonical format declaration. A contract cannot promise execution for an asset shape that the same format rejects structurally.
x-adcp-validation.layer_derivation: Publisher, placement, and seller effective-contract derivation is evaluated over atomic tuples of normalized non-version selector identity, one exact version (or null for pixel), execution_actor, and one firing_path. For a complete parent, every child tuple MUST exist in the parent, the child remains complete, and array compression MUST NOT create a version/path cross-product. An incomplete or omitted parent is not a ceiling: a child may add or omit affirmative tuples for its narrower scope, but remains incomplete until every applicable layer is complete. Omission from an incomplete child is undeclared, not an assertion that the tuple is unsupported.
x-adcp-validation.cardinality: Each accepted manifest tracker instance is initiated exactly once in total for each logical event occurrence; identical URLs are not deduplicated.

verifier_constraints.adcp_semantic_identity: when dialect is adcp, dialect_semantic must equal universal_semantic
verifier_constraints.translation_chain: a translate_to_native entry is usable only when the same capability set contains an exact resolve_value entry for translation_target

verifier_constraints.ctv_experience_matrix: ctv_ad_experience on image must be pause or screensaver
verifier_constraints.motion_level_static_canonical: motion_level full_motion is rejected on image
verifier_constraints.ctv_activation_copy_slots: push_notification activation_methods SHOULD declare an activation_message slot; text_message SHOULD declare an activation_text_message slot; email SHOULD declare activation_email_subject and activation_email_body slots. Missing copy slots emit a non-blocking validate_input warnings[] entry.

external:formats/canonical/_base.json.x-canonical-policy-required-params-not-e: Canonical format schemas intentionally do NOT mark parameter fields as required and use additionalProperties: true. The canonical describes which parameters MAY narrow a declaration; it does not supply hidden technical defaults. When a technical parameter is omitted, its meaning comes only from the enclosing declaration's technical_requirements_complete assertion: true means no constraint at that layer, while false or absence means undeclared. Consumers MUST NOT infer an omitted technical constraint from canonical prose, examples, common practice, or implementation defaults. This is intentional: structural schema validation and product-level technical-contract completeness are separate checks.
external:formats/canonical/_base.json.x-adcp-file-size-units: Creative file-size fields ending in `_kb` use exactly 1,000 bytes per KB. Fields ending in `_mb` use exactly 1,000,000 bytes per MB. Fields ending in `_bytes` are exact byte counts.

verifier_constraints.ctv_experience_matrix: ctv_ad_experience on video_hosted must be screensaver
ctv_ad_experience on video_vast must be one of pause, screensaver, overlay, squeezeback, in_scene, with creative_type nonlinear
verifier_constraints.ctv_nonlinear_no_simid: Every video_vast CTV experience is nonlinear and forbids simid_supported true because VAST serializes InteractiveCreativeFile only under Linear MediaFiles
verifier_constraints.ctv_duration_floors: overlay and squeezeback require duration_ms_exact or duration_ms_range minimum of at least 10000; in_scene at least 3000; pause has no floor
verifier_constraints.ctv_activation_copy_slots: push_notification activation_methods SHOULD declare an activation_message slot; text_message SHOULD declare an activation_text_message slot; email SHOULD declare activation_email_subject and activation_email_body slots. Missing copy slots emit a non-blocking validate_input warnings[] entry.
verifier_constraints.creative_type_precedence: creative_type wins over linear_required when both are declared; linear_required true with creative_type nonlinear or either is a contradiction and is rejected

verifier_constraints.range_order: When both bounds are declared, min_width MUST be <= max_width, min_height MUST be <= max_height, and min_bitrate_kbps MUST be <= max_bitrate_kbps.
verifier_constraints.adaptive_bitrate_containment: A MediaFile advertising a minBitrate/maxBitrate interval satisfies declared bitrate bounds only when its entire interval is contained within those bounds; overlap alone is insufficient.
verifier_constraints.alternative_renditions: For each applicable resolved InLine linear creative, at least one MediaFile MUST satisfy every declared property in this object; requirements MUST NOT be satisfied by combining properties from different MediaFile elements.
verifier_constraints.missing_metadata: If a declared property cannot be established from VAST metadata or safe inspection, compatibility is unproven and the MediaFile does not satisfy that property.

verifier_constraints.audio_profile: The resolved InLine creative MUST be Linear and supply a playable audio MediaFile; VAST 4.1+ documents MUST declare Ad adType audio. Video and hybrid ads do not satisfy audio_vast.
verifier_constraints.audio_media_files: Every playable MediaFile used to satisfy the declaration MUST have an audio/* MIME type and the VAST-required width and height values of 0.
verifier_constraints.audio_version_compatibility: VAST 4.1+ is the standards-conformant audio profile. A seller accepts 2.0, 3.0, or 4.0 only by listing that version explicitly as legacy audio interoperability.

verifier_constraints.ctv_experience_matrix: ctv_ad_experience on sponsored_placement must be menu, squeezeback, or in_scene
ctv_ad_experience on native_in_feed must be menu or overlay
verifier_constraints.menu_profile_fields: menu_placement and focus_behavior require ctv_ad_experience menu
verifier_constraints.focus_video_pairing: focus_behavior autoplay_muted or autoplay_sound requires the effective slots to include the video asset group
verifier_constraints.ctv_activation_copy_slots: push_notification activation_methods SHOULD declare an activation_message slot; text_message SHOULD declare an activation_text_message slot; email SHOULD declare activation_email_subject and activation_email_body slots. Missing copy slots emit a non-blocking validate_input warnings[] entry.

verifier_constraints.initial_state_resolution: initial_state_id must resolve to a declared state
verifier_constraints.single_state_shape: when states has one entry, transitions must be absent or empty and initial_state_id must equal the sole state; when states has more than one entry, transitions must be present and non-empty
verifier_constraints.transition_exit_determinism: at most one transition out of a given state per cause tuple (trigger, plus input for user_action, media_event for media_event, direction for scroll_threshold); distinct causes may coexist and the seller runtime arms whichever inputs the device supports
verifier_constraints.transition_state_resolution: transition endpoints must resolve to distinct declared states
verifier_constraints.scroll_progress_bounds: scroll_start_percent must be less than scroll_end_percent
verifier_constraints.scroll_linked_binding: transition_mode scroll_linked is valid only with trigger scroll_progress
verifier_constraints.state_reachability: every non-initial state must be reachable from initial_state_id
verifier_constraints.timer_cycle_floor: timer and in_view_timer transitions participating in a state cycle must declare delay_ms >= 1000
verifier_constraints.dismissibility_floor: any state anchored overlay or fullscreen_overlay requires user_controls.dismissible true or that state's close_affordance true
verifier_constraints.breakpoint_id_uniqueness: breakpoints[].breakpoint_id values must be unique within each state
verifier_constraints.width_range_order: width_range minimum must be less than or equal to maximum
verifier_constraints.height_range_order: height_range minimum must be less than or equal to maximum
verifier_constraints.aspect_consistency: canvas_aspect_ratio must be consistent with fixed width and height when both are declared
verifier_constraints.duration_ms_range_order: duration_ms_range[0] must be less than or equal to duration_ms_range[1] when both are non-null
verifier_constraints.motion_animation_bound: max_animation_s is required when a state's motion is animated and forbidden when static
verifier_constraints.slot_binding_resolution: states[].slot_bindings values must resolve to declared slot asset_group_ids
verifier_constraints.allowed_slot_asset_types: declaration slots (including params.slots overrides) must not widen the canonical's allowed asset types; executable types are rejected
verifier_constraints.supply_mode_manifest: components mode forbids state_canvases and layered_source assets; rendered_canvases mode requires full canvas coverage and forbids layered_source; layered_source mode requires a layered_source asset and forbids state_canvases
verifier_constraints.fluid_breakpoint_supply: breakpoints using width_mode or viewport_height_percent cannot be targeted by rendered_canvases supply
verifier_constraints.state_canvas_coverage: in rendered_canvases mode, exactly one state_canvases image per declared state and breakpoint pair
verifier_constraints.state_canvas_dimensions: canvas width must equal declared width or fall within width_range; height must equal fixed height or fall within height_range
verifier_constraints.state_canvas_extras: undeclared and duplicate state/breakpoint pairs are rejected
verifier_constraints.clickthrough_policy: landing_page_url required when clickthrough is required; landing_page_url and state_click_urls forbidden when clickthrough is none
verifier_constraints.state_click_url_resolution: state_click_urls entries must carry state_id resolving to a declared state, with at most one entry per state
verifier_constraints.lean_policy_warnings: non-user-action transitions into overlay/fullscreen_overlay anchoring, hover-triggered expansion, and scroll transitions into overlay anchoring emit policy warnings (non-blocking)

verifier_constraints.selector_resolution: state_id and breakpoint_id resolve against the containing seller_rendered_stateful_display declaration; coordinated_placements component constraints omit both selectors
verifier_constraints.region_bounds: percent regions satisfy x + width <= 100 and y + height <= 100; pixel regions fit within every selected canvas

verifier_constraints.required_component: at least one component must be required
verifier_constraints.placement_ref_resolution: components[].placement_ref values must resolve to distinct Product.placements[] entries
verifier_constraints.format_option_ref_resolution: component references resolve only against sibling format_options entries on the same product
verifier_constraints.component_kind: resolved and inline components cannot be custom or coordinated_placements
verifier_constraints.inline_params: inline params validate against the schema selected by inline format_kind
verifier_constraints.component_assets: required components have a component_assets entry satisfying their resolved canonical slots
verifier_constraints.sequence_values: when any component declares sequence, sequence values must start at 1 and be contiguous across the declared set
verifier_constraints.referenced_option_schema: declarations resolved via format_option_ref are schema-validated identically to inline params
verifier_constraints.shared_slot_consumers: every shared_slots[].consumed_by value resolves to a declared component_id whose canonical slots accept the shared asset_group_id and asset_type
